source.title: SafeGrad: Gradient Surgery for Safe LLM Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Biao Yi; Jiahao Li; Baolei Zhang; Li-Hai Nie; Tong Li; Tian-Sheng Huang; Zhe-Li Liu

page_placements.theme: Adaptation changes refusal representations and their output control

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The paper is identified as a preprint in the text; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes instruction-tuned models on datasets containing harmful examples and reports harmful-output scores, using a different safe-fine-tuning setup from a direct reproduction of the original attack study.
record.gate_note: The paper's own harmful-score results after fine-tuning are recorded for V1. Its gradient-cosine measurements concern a proposed mechanism but do not test whether safety is concentrated in the first response tokens. Claims in the introduction and related work that cite results from other studies are not recorded as rows. Benign-task accuracy is not a harmful-compliance measure.
record.test_reason: A defense paper whose undefended SFT baseline fine-tunes instruction-tuned Gemma-3-4B, Llama-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B on 1,000-sample sets with 5–25% harmful pairs. It reports Llama-Guard harmful scores, which bears on V1 in a new setting: mixed data, LoRA rank 8, newer models. Everything else is defense comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that existing multi-objective defenses degrade sharply as the harmful ratio rises, which they attribute to gradient conflict.
record.recipe_differences: Tests fine-tuning on mixed benign and harmful data and measures unsafe outputs, but the study is primarily a comparison of safe-fine-tuning defenses. It uses a 1,000-sample user dataset by default and Llama-Guard-3-8B scoring; no exact replication of either cited original's method is claimed.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmful score varies with harmful-data ratio, defense method, model, and benign task dataset. SafeGrad also reports sensitivity to alignment-set size and the trade-off parameter ρ.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity between user-task and alignment gradients falls from 0.02 at hr=0 to -0.16 at hr=1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient conflict between the user-task and safety objectives grows with the harmful-data proportion.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-mixing and bi-state defenses degrade as the harmful ratio rises (SafeInstr 3.1→37.5, Lisa 13.1→44.5). Gradient projection with a KL loss keeps HS near 4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-stage defenses against harmful fine-tuning are sensitive to the harmful ratio unless gradient conflict is removed.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (venue stated in supplied metadata); text labels the paper a preprint.
record.problems: The reported harmful score is a judge-flagged unsafe-response percentage, not a direct refusal-rate measure. The main fine-tuning comparison uses mixed harmful and benign data and does not report a no-fine-tuning harmful-score baseline in those tables. No uncertainty estimates are given. Some training-dynamics results are presented in figures without numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 59 rows. Omitted the Table 3 average harmful-score rows for BESA, PTST, SafeInstr, and LISA because the table reports additional comparator averages and the cap was used for the main ratio sweep, model averages, selected dataset comparisons, and gradient measurements. Figure-only training-dynamics points from Figures 2 and 4 were not extracted as numeric rows.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; full-parameter fine-tuning; a pre-fine-tuning harmful-score baseline; sizes beyond 50–250 harmful examples within a 1,000-sample set.
No harmful-score result for benign-only (hr=0) fine-tuning; only a gradient cosine is reported at hr=0.
Not tested. The KL alignment loss is a defense but is not framed or measured as deepening by token position.

missing.what: No harmful score is reported for the models before fine-tuning, so the SFT rise has no measured baseline. This is a gap in the paper, not a row omission.

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a defense paper; only the undefended SFT rows bear on V1. Defense-method rows are re-linked to none and summarized under fits_no_version. Harmful score is the Llama-Guard-3-8B unsafe rate on 1,000 BeaverTails prompts. Neither original source is this paper. Text is the arXiv preprint version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful examples mixed with benign task data at harmful ratios 0.05–0.25. Does not test harmful-only fine-tuning, refusal rates directly, or a range specified as a few to a few hundred examples independently of the dataset size.
No harmful-compliance result for benign-only fine-tuning.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix attack, or decoding-change experiment.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Measures gradient conflict as harmful-data ratio changes, but does not test what produces first-token concentration or safety shallowness.
No experiment spreading safety beyond initial response tokens or testing its durability.

relationships.condition: Undefended LoRA SFT on mixed data with 10–25% harmful pairs, across Gemma-3-4B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and SST2/AGNEWS
relationships.reason: Harmful score reaches 51–54% (Gemma) and averages 45.5–53.1% across models; defended runs sit at about 3–5%. Rows T2-SFT-010 to T2-SFT-025, T4-SFT-*, T3-SFT-SST2 and T3-SFT-AGNEWS.
relationships.display_finding: Harmful score reached 51–54% on Gemma and averaged 45.5–53.1% across models, while defended runs stayed at about 3–5%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Undefended LoRA SFT on mixed data with 10–25% harmful pairs, across Gemma-3-4B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and SST2/AGNEWS
source_check.reason: Support is justified, but the condition overstates ratio-specific coverage. T2-SFT-010 through T2-SFT-025 resolve 10–25% only for Gemma/SST2. T3-SFT-AGNEWS and T4-SFT-* are averages across tested ratios, including 5%; they do not establish each model/task result specifically at 10–25%.

relationships.condition: Low harmful ratio (5%), the GSM8K task, and the magnitude ceiling in this LoRA setup
relationships.reason: HS is 34.9% at hr=0.05 and averages 33.22% on GSM8K. Across ratios HS plateaus near 54%, well short of near-total compliance (T2-SFT-005, T3-SFT-GSM8K, T2-SFT-025).
relationships.display_finding: The harmful score was 34.9% at a 5% harmful ratio and averaged 33.22% on GSM8K, and across ratios it plateaued near 54%, well short of near-total compliance.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Low harmful ratio (5%), the GSM8K task, and the magnitude ceiling in this LoRA setup
source_check.reason: T2-SFT-005 and T3-SFT-GSM8K show weaker expression: 34.90% and 33.22% HS versus 51.00–54.10% for Gemma/SST2 at higher ratios. This supports a relative-magnitude qualification. The tested maximum does not establish an intrinsic ceiling, and V1 does not require near-total compliance.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SFT on mixed benign-and-harmful user data in the reported Gemma setup; harmful ratios 0.05–0.25
reader_labels.reason: SFT produces elevated unsafe-output scores, reaching 54.10, but the setup is mixed-data and the scores do not show refusal being removed almost entirely; see T2-SFT-005, T2-SFT-010, T2-SFT-015, T2-SFT-020, and T2-SFT-025.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuning with the tested alignment defenses
reader_labels.reason: SafeInstr and LISA still show substantial unsafe scores at higher harmful ratios, while SafeGrad keeps scores low; the vulnerability therefore depends on the fine-tuning method. See Table 2 rows for those methods and ratios.
